transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
My ankles have been swollen, both of them, and it's been going on for about four weeks now. By the end of the day my shoes feel tight, though they're usually back to normal in the morning.
When did you first notice it?
About four weeks ago. It came on gradually, and I noticed by the evening my ankles were puffy.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's worse as the day goes on — by teatime my shoes feel tight — and it's mostly gone in the morning after I've been lying flat. My socks leave marks on the skin too.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?

It's mildly uncomfortable, about a 3 out of 10 — mostly it's just that my ankles look puffy and my shoes feel tight by the end of the day. The swelling is in both ankles and up my lower shins, about equally.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
It's in both ankles and up into my lower shins, about the same on both sides. It doesn't go any higher than that.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
About a 3 out of 10 — it's mildly uncomfortable rather than painful.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — it builds up during the day, worse by the evening, and it's mostly gone in the morning after I've been lying flat.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
Nothing else has really been bothering me. I've not had any breathlessness when lying flat, no waking up breathless in the night, and no chest pain. There's also no pain or redness in either calf.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I have high blood pressure, and I've been told my kidney function is a bit reduced.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I take amlodipine for my blood pressure — that was increased from 5 mg to 10 mg once daily about six weeks ago. I also take a small water tablet each morning, though I can't remember its name, and simvastatin 20 mg at night.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, I don't have any known allergies to medicines.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
I've been sitting with my feet up in the afternoons, and I've stopped wearing my usual shoes because they feel too tight. Otherwise I'm managing my usual activities.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes, it does worry me. I'm afraid the swelling might mean my heart is failing — my sister had heart failure, so it's on my mind.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
